what: Bilibili is a Chinese video platform popular with young people, known for anime, gaming and user-made videos with on-screen comments. It earns money from advertising, mobile games, value-added services such as memberships and live streaming, and e-commerce.
customers: Hundreds of millions of young Chinese users, advertisers, and game players.
money: Premium memberships, live-streaming tips and other paid features.
moat: A loyal, young community that creates much of the content itself, which is hard for rivals to copy.
risks: Competition from Douyin and Kuaishou for young users and advertisers.
Chinese regulation of games and online content.
Profit only turned positive in 2025 after years of large losses.
US-listed Chinese stocks carry geopolitical risk.
opportunities: Gross profit nearly tripled from $558M in 2022 to $1.59B in 2025.
Free cash flow of $949M in 2025, and cash of $3.6B against $1.4B of debt.
At about 9 times forward earnings, the shares are cheap if profits keep rising.
Twenty-nine analysts rate it a strong buy with an average target near $23, about double the price.
watch: Advertising growth and gaming hits, and whether margins keep expanding.
view: Bilibili has turned from a cash-burning platform into a profitable one: gross profit nearly tripled since 2022 and free cash flow reached almost $950 million in 2025. Yet at about 9 times forward earnings and with net cash, the shares trade like a business in decline.

The discount reflects the usual worries about Chinese internet stocks, regulation and competition from Douyin, plus scepticism that the profit turnaround will last. Those risks are real, but the improvement has been steady for three years.

This turns on whether margins keep expanding. I think the turnaround is genuine and the valuation too low, but investors must accept China risk. Analysts’ average target near double the price shows how cheap it looks.
bull: Advertising and games grow, margins keep rising and the market re-rates a profitable platform.
bear: Competition and regulation stall growth and Chinese stocks stay out of favour.
